title: Pointer-Based Buffer
statement: Design a 4-entry buffer with separate write and read pointers and full/empty indicators. Writes should advance the write pointer and reads advance the read pointer on the clock. The buffer must be circular and handle simultaneous write/read correctly.
module_signature: module pointer_based_buffer(input clk, input rst, input write_en, input read_en, input [7:0] din, output reg [7:0] dout, output reg full, output reg empty);
behavior: write_en stores din when full is 0.
read_en outputs the next value when empty is 0.
All state updates occur on the rising edge of clk.
rst is active-high and synchronous unless the problem statement explicitly says otherwise.
Use non-blocking assignments in clocked always blocks.
Outputs must never depend on uninitialized x/z state after reset.
When rst is asserted on a rising edge, registered outputs reset to their documented initial values.
constraints: Do not use external queue primitives.
example:
write_en read_en | full empty dout
1 0 | 0 0 xx
0 1 | 0 0 stored
hint: Maintain write/read pointers and count entries.
